deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematical content on this page. It is a library request or loan slip of the kind used at the Göttingen University Library. In ink, in a librarian's or clerk's hand: 'Th. Young. Natural philosophy. London. 1807. 2 vol. 4°'. This identifies Thomas Young, 'A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts' (London: J. Johnson, 1807, 2 vols, quarto). Below it, in pencil and probably in Riemann's own hand, the title is written out more fully: 'Young a course of lectures on' with 'and the mechanical arts' added above and bracketed into the line. Then come 'V. 1. 2' (volumes 1 and 2 requested) and a large pencil '2', apparently a count of volumes or a desk mark, with a long pencil stroke crossing the lower part of the slip, likely marking the loan as returned or cancelled. Further marks: a red-ink note at lower left, probably a date ('Jan. 26 …', year illegible) or a clerk's annotation; the borrower's signature 'B. Riemann' at lower right, with a bracketed word beneath it, probably a residence or address note, reading uncertain; the archival marks 'Riemann 2' (top right) and the folio number '42'. Context: Young's Lectures contain his wave theory of light and interference, his elasticity theory (Young's modulus), capillarity and acoustics. This fits Riemann's documented interests in mathematical physics: his natural-philosophy fragments, his work on the mechanics of the ear, and electrodynamics and light. The slip only documents that he borrowed or requested the book.

results.what: Record that Riemann requested/borrowed Thomas Young's 'A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts' (1807), vols 1-2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a library loan slip with no mathematics. That Riemann read the standard physics literature (Young on light, elasticity and acoustics) is unsurprising, given his known work in mathematical physics. At most it is a minor biographical datum about his reading.
transcription_corrections: 'Riemann 2.' is an archival mark at top right, not part of the slip's text.

The pencil line reads 'Young a course of lectures on' with the insertion 'and the mechanical arts' written above and bracketed into it; together they give the full title 'A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts'.
'42' is the archival folio number at the right margin, not content.
The red-ink annotation at lower left is only partially legible ('Jan. 26…'?); the year and remainder are uncertain, and it may be a clerk's date stamp.
The word in parentheses under 'B. Riemann' is uncertain: 'Weppel' is a guess, and 'Wispel' or similar is equally possible. It is probably an address or residence note.
The large pencil '2' and the long crossing pencil stroke are library or clerical marks (volume count; cancellation or return), not mathematical symbols.
